territorial_scope.description: Applies to federal executive agencies and their procurement of LLMs; vendors are reached through required contract terms.

evidence.quote: procure only those LLMs developed in accordance with the following two principles

summary.short: Directs federal agency heads to procure only large language models that meet two Unbiased AI Principles (truth-seeking and ideological neutrality), with OMB guidance due within 120 days of the order dated July 23, 2025.
summary.long: The order requires federal agency heads, consistent with applicable law, to procure only large language models (LLMs) developed under two Unbiased AI Principles: truth-seeking (truthful responses to factual prompts, prioritising historical accuracy and acknowledging uncertainty) and ideological neutrality (no manipulation of responses in favour of ideological dogmas such as DEI, and no intentional encoding of partisan or ideological judgments unless prompted or readily accessible to end users). Within 120 days the Director of OMB must issue implementing guidance, which must account for technical limitations, allow vendors to show transparency through system prompts, specifications, evaluations or other documentation, and make exceptions for national security systems. Agency heads must include contract terms requiring compliance in new LLM contracts, charge decommissioning costs to vendors terminated for noncompliance after a reasonable cure period, revise existing contracts where practicable, and within 90 days of the OMB guidance adopt compliance procedures. The order does not impair existing agency authority, is subject to appropriations, and creates no enforceable rights.

notes: No registry IDs were supplied, so all target_instrument_id values are blank. Sec. 3 limits the Unbiased AI Principles to procurement of LLMs, while Sec. 4(a)(iv) lets agency heads consider applying them to AI models other than LLMs. Sec. 4(b) duties apply 'to the maximum extent consistent with applicable law', and Sec. 5(b) makes the order subject to appropriations. Sec. 5(c) states that the order creates no enforceable right. No enforcement provision is stated.

thresholds.note: The order sets no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. Its only numbers are procedural time limits (120 days for OMB guidance in Sec. 4(a); 90 days for agency procedures in Sec. 4(b)(iii)), which are coded as deadline events, and citations to other instruments (Executive Order 13960 of December 3, 2020; 5 U.S.C. 101, 102, 104(1); 31 U.S.C. 9101; 44 U.S.C. 3552(b)(6)). Sec. 4(b)(i) and Sec. 4(b)(iii) refer to 'the date of the OMB guidance' rather than to a numeric cutoff.
